problem.statement: Make two-agent Intent Document distillation installable and enforceable with client-specific roles, server-side capability separation, and better transcript selection and retrieval.
out_of_scope: No qualifying underlying-work transcript was found; original scope and evolution are unknown.

assumptions.assumption: REVIEW_ASSIST_ROLE plus generated client configuration enforce the intended author/reviewer boundary.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: One context could access both transcripts and submission.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Enumerate and invoke tools under installed author and reviewer configurations.

assumptions.assumption: Leading XML-like blocks are injected scaffolding, not user content.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Legitimate asks can disappear from previews and classification.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Test injected wrappers and legitimate leading markup.

assumptions.assumption: SERVER_VERSION remains synchronized with release metadata.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: CLI and package versions can disagree.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Compare them during release or automate the check.

assumptions.assumption: Markdown/TOML loaders and published agent files work in npm and MCPB artifacts.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Generated roles can be unavailable after distribution.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Pack, inspect, install, and exercise both artifacts.

requirements.text: Separate transcript access from Intent Document submission at the registered-tool boundary.
Generate shared author/reviewer roles for Claude, Codex, and generic clients.
Distinguish work sessions from distillation runs and retrieve question-specific transcript passages.
Ship role assets and CLI installation/version entry points.

adopted.summary: Add shared role prose and client wrappers, a rendering registry, REVIEW_ASSIST_ROLE registration gating, agent CLI support, and transcript preview/search enhancements.
adopted.rationale: Inferred from code: shared prose limits drift, server gating enforces separation, and targeted search reduces author context. No transcript confirms rationale or rejected alternatives.

tour.title: Canonical role protocol
tour.what: Defines author, reviewer, and mandatory baseline questions.
tour.why: Establishes custody, submission, interviewing, and uncertainty rules.

tour.title: Client-specific wrappers
tour.what: Wraps shared roles for Claude, Codex, and generic clients.
tour.why: Adapts the protocol to client configuration and permission models.

tour.title: Role registry
tour.what: Renders roles, detects clients, declares install metadata and tool partitions.
tour.why: Keeps prose shared while producing environment-native definitions.

tour.title: Server enforcement and CLI
tour.what: Gates tool registration by role; adds role retrieval, agent installation, version CLI, and active-role reporting.
tour.why: Makes the split enforceable and distributable.
tour.attention: Runtime partitions lack recovered test evidence.

tour.title: Transcript selection and search
tour.what: Cleans first-user previews, flags probable distillation runs, and adds ranked transcript search.
tour.why: Helps authors choose the work session and retrieve passages relevant to one question.
tour.attention: Markup stripping risks false removal; search loads the full file despite streaming rationale.

tour.title: Required two-agent guide
tour.what: Requires obtaining role definitions before separate author/reviewer runs.

tour.title: Package role assets
tour.what: Publishes agents and configures text loaders and TypeScript declarations.
tour.why: Makes source templates available to builds and packages.

not_verified: No qualifying work transcript exists, so no build, lint, typecheck, test, CLI, packaging, or manual verification can be claimed.
Problem evolution, rejected alternatives, exact scope, cross-client role behavior, transcript edge cases, artifact contents, and version consistency remain unverified.
